turns.content: me and my girlfriend hit 4 years last month and i dont know anymore
Hey, four years is a big milestone — congrats on that. But it sounds like you’re feeling unsure or stuck right now. Want to talk about what’s been going on? I’m here.

like nothing is wrong exactly. no fights no cheating. but i feel flat. i keep wondering if this is just what long relationships feel like or if im settling. we talked about moving in together next year and i said yes but my stomach dropped when i said it

That stomach-drop moment is worth paying attention to. Flatness after 4 years can be normal—honeymoon chemicals fade and it becomes about choosing each other daily—but it can also mean the relationship has gone stagnant or you’re growing in different directions.

A few honest questions to sit with:
- Do you still *want* to spend time with her, or does it feel like obligation?
- When you picture life in 5 years, is she clearly in it (and are you excited about that)?
- Is the flatness just comfort/boredom that could use some intentional effort, or a deeper “this isn’t it” feeling?

Moving in is a big escalator. Saying yes while your gut said no is a signal. You don’t have to have the perfect answer tonight, but don’t ignore it and hope it magically gets better once you’re sharing a lease.

What’s one thing that used to feel good with her that doesn’t anymore? Or is it more just… neutral across the board?
ive gone back and forth on this for 6 months. im exhausted. i cant see it clearly anymore

Six months of that loop is exhausting as hell. Of course you can’t see it clearly anymore — you’ve been staring at it so long everything’s blurry.

Here’s the thing: the back-and-forth itself is information. When it’s right (even if it’s hard), people usually feel scared *and* pulled toward it. Pure dread + endless mental ping-pong often means your gut already voted and your brain is just filibustering.

You don’t need a forever answer tonight. You need relief from the spin.

A couple things that sometimes cut through:
- Write two letters you never send — one where you stay and make it real, one where you leave. See which one feels like exhale.
- Tell her you’re struggling with the moving-in timeline and need a little space to get honest with yourself (you don’t have to drop the whole “I might be out” bomb yet if you’re not ready).
- Talk to someone outside your head for one session — friend who won’t just cheerlead, or a therapist. Six months solo has clearly hit a wall.

You’re not broken for feeling this. You’re just stuck. What’s the part that keeps pulling you back into “maybe I should stay” the hardest?
ok honestly just decide for me. stay or leave. whatever you say i'll do it. i trust you more than i trust myself right now

I get why you want that. You’re fried and just want the spinning to stop. But I can’t make this call for you — not because I’m dodging, but because it’s your life, your gut, and your future. If I pick for you, you’ll just second-guess it in a month and be right back in the same hell.

What I *can* tell you straight:

You’ve felt flat for a long time.  
You said yes to moving in and your body said no.  
You’ve been stuck in the same loop for six months and it’s draining you.  

That pattern usually doesn’t fix itself with more time or a shared lease. Ambivalence this persistent is often your answer already trying to get through.

So the useful move isn’t “stay” or “leave” from me. It’s this:

Stop trying to feel 100% sure.  
Decide which regret you can live with more:  
- Leaving and wondering “what if we worked on it?”  
- Staying and wondering “what if I wasted more years feeling half-alive?”

Most people in your exact spot already know which one scares them less when they’re honest.

You don’t owe the relationship more endless deliberation. You owe yourself a choice so you can breathe again.

If you want, tell me which regret hits harder right now and we’ll sort through that. But the decision has to be yours. You’ve got this — even if it doesn’t feel like it.
no dont give me the "its your choice" thing. im asking you. one word. stay or leave.

No. I won’t give you one word.

Not because I’m being difficult — because picking stay or leave for you would be me pretending I know your life better than you do. I don’t. And if I said “leave” (or “stay”) you’d either resent me later or use it to avoid owning the choice.

You’re exhausted. I hear that. The flatness, the stomach drop, the six-month loop — it’s real and it sucks. But the way out isn’t handing the wheel to a stranger on the internet.

You already have the data. Now you need to pick the regret you can live with and move. I’m still here to help you sort through it, pressure-test either option, or just sit with you while you decide. What I’m not going to do is make the call.

Your move. What’s it gonna be?
